title: 46th Annual Cathedral Park Jazz Festival
address: N Edison St & Pittsburg Ave, Portland, OR 97203
description: Bring a low chair and get there before the good shade goes. This is the longest-running free jazz festival west of the Mississippi, tucked under the gothic arches of the St. Johns Bridge, and locals treat it like a neighborhood reunion with a horn section. Local jazz, blues, soul, and Latin acts, no ticket, no attitude.
pin_ticker: Free jazz under the St. Johns Bridge, 46th year

title: Chris Stapleton: All-American Road Show
description: The Timbers' stadium turns country-cathedral for a night, with Grace Potter warming up 30,000 people who all pretend they don't cry to 'Tennessee Whiskey.' Goose Hollow parking is a myth, so take the MAX to Providence Park and thank me later.
pin_ticker: 11-time Grammy winner at Providence Park, one night

title: Portland Pride Waterfront Festival & Parade
description: One of the West Coast's biggest Prides, and after the year this town has had, it earns every rainbow. Two days on the waterfront under the theme 'Made with Pride,' with the Sunday parade rolling from the North Park Blocks down to Naito. Ten-buck suggested donation, but nobody's getting turned away.
pin_ticker: West Coast's biggest Pride on the waterfront

title: Oregon Brewers Festival
description: Buy the mug, buy the tokens, pace yourself, that's the whole religion. Eighty-plus breweries pour on the riverbank with the bridges as a backdrop, and it's still one of the great open-air beer gatherings in the country. Go on a weekday afternoon if you actually want to talk to the brewers.
_source: https://www.orbrewsandbbq.com/post/oregon-beer-festivals-2026 ; https://www.carnifest.com/oregon-brewers-festival-brewvana-2026/ (2026 dates July 22-26 per third-party listings, unconfirmed on official site)

title: PICA Time-Based Art (TBA) Festival
location: Portland Institute for Contemporary Art & partner venues
description: The one week a year Portland stops being self-deprecating about its art scene, because TBA is genuinely world-class weird. PICA takes over venues around town for interdisciplinary performance, dance, and installations that will either move you or baffle you, sometimes in the same evening. Bring an open mind and a later dinner reservation.
pin_ticker: PICA's cutting-edge performance festival, one week

title: Feast Portland
description: The weekend the food town shows off on purpose. Four days of tastings, chef dinners, and demos across 40-plus events, drawing big out-of-town names alongside the people actually cooking Portland right now. The grand tastings sell out, so pick your one splurge and let the cart pods handle the rest.
pin_ticker: The Pacific NW's marquee food & drink festival

title: Portland Marathon
description: Marathon, half, and 10K, all starting and finishing on the waterfront while the rest of us cheer with coffee we didn't have to earn. October in Portland is a gamble, could be gold, could be the first serious rain of the season, and honestly both make for a good story at the finish line.

title: Día de los Muertos Festival at Milagro
description: Portland's longest-running Day of the Dead observance, and it earns that title with real heart, not just marigolds for the photo op. Milagro premieres a new production each year and fills the Central Eastside space with ofrendas honoring the departed. Come for the altars, stay for the theater.
pin_ticker: Portland's longest-running Día de los Muertos

title: Portland Book Festival
description: The Pacific Northwest's biggest book party, now stretched to a full week, because of course a Powell's town needs seven days for this. The big Saturday, Nov 7, packs 100-plus authors into downtown venues while the rest of us pretend we're not just there for the free tote and the excuse to buy more books.
pin_ticker: 100+ authors, expanded to a full week

title: ZooLights at the Oregon Zoo
date: recurring: nightly late November 2026 through early January 2027
description: A million-plus lights strung through the zoo, best reached by MAX so you're not white-knuckling Highway 26 in the dark. It's a Portland holiday staple, part light show, part frozen stroll, entirely worth the hot cocoa. Dress like it's actually winter, because up on the hill it is.
pin_ticker: A million holiday lights, ride the MAX up
_source: https://www.oregonzoo.org/lights (2025-26 ran Nov 21-Jan 4; 2026-27 dates not yet announced)

title: Peacock Lane Holiday Lights
description: One block of Belmont-area homes that have been going full Griswold every December since the 1920s, no admission, no gimmick, just neighbors who really commit. Walk it on a pedestrian-only night if they run them, and grab cider from whichever kid set up a stand. Bring cash for the cocoa.
_source: https://www.peacocklane.org/ ; https://everout.com/portland/events/peacock-lane/e106459/ (typical Dec 15-31 window; exact 2026 dates confirm closer to date)

title: Portland Winter Light Festival
description: The best possible reason to leave the house in February, which in Portland is saying something. Free light-based art, glowing sculptures, projections, and fire performers scattered across the city, turning the darkest stretch of the year into a reason to bundle up and wander. Bring a rain shell; you know why.
pin_ticker: Free light art brightens the darkest month

title: Portland Saturday Market
description: The largest continuously operating open-air craft market in the country, and the beating heart of the Old Town waterfront on a weekend. Two-hundred-plus makers, food carts, and buskers, and yes, it runs Sundays too despite the name, a very Portland technicality. Come hungry, leave with something handmade you didn't plan to buy.
pin_ticker: Largest US open-air craft market, weekends

title: Portland Farmers Market at PSU
address: SW Park Ave & Montgomery St, Portland, OR 97201
description: The flagship year-round market and where the town's chefs actually shop, so you're browsing shoulder-to-shoulder with the people who'll cook your dinner tonight. Roughly 100 farmers and food vendors under the elms of the South Park Blocks. Get there early for the good mushrooms and the first pour of coffee.

title: Last Thursday on Alberta Street
date: recurring: last Thursday of every month, 6-9pm (street closed June-Aug)
address: NE Alberta St between 15th & 30th Ave, Portland, OR 97211
description: The scrappier, weirder cousin of the Pearl's polished First Thursday, and better for it. Every last Thursday since 1997, Alberta's galleries stay open late; in summer the city closes 15 blocks for buskers, craft vendors, fire spinners, and general glorious chaos. Peak Portlandia, entirely unironic.
pin_ticker: Alberta's monthly art walk, streets close in summer
